basic_information.name: Operator / Computer Use / Agentic Browsers
basic_information.creator: Multiple: OpenAI (Operator, CUA, Atlas), Anthropic (Computer Use, Claude for Chrome), Google DeepMind (Project Mariner), Perplexity (Comet), The Browser Company / Atlassian (Dia), Microsoft (Edge Copilot), Opera (Neon)
basic_information.release_date: October 2024 (Anthropic Computer Use beta), January 2025 (OpenAI Operator), May 2025 (Project Mariner rollout), June 2025 (Dia beta), July 2025 (Comet launch), October 2025 (ChatGPT Atlas)
basic_information.license: Proprietary (all major products). Open-source alternatives exist: Open Operator (Browserbase, MIT), Openator (open-source), Agent S (open-source), browser-use (open-source)
basic_information.current_version: OpenAI CUA (computer_use_preview in Responses API), Anthropic Computer Use (computer_20251124 for Opus 4.5+, computer_20250124 for other models), Project Mariner (Gemini 2.5-powered, multi-task update May 2025), Comet (free tier + Max tier, Android added Nov 2025), Atlas (macOS, agent mode Jan 2026), Dia (acquired by Atlassian Oct 2025)

technical_architecture.architecture_pattern: single_agent with GUI interaction loop. All products share a common pattern: screenshot capture -> vision model interpretation -> action generation (mouse/keyboard) -> execution -> verification loop. Some support multi-task parallelism (Mariner handles up to 10 simultaneous tasks, Comet spawns parallel browser agents).
technical_architecture.underlying_models: OpenAI Operator/Atlas: CUA model built on GPT-4o with vision + reinforcement learning for GUI interaction. Anthropic Computer Use: Claude Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, Opus 4.6 (with enhanced zoom action). Google Mariner: Gemini 2.0/2.5. Perplexity Comet: Perplexity's proprietary models. Dia: Multi-model (uses various LLM providers). Microsoft Edge Copilot: GPT-4o via Copilot Studio.
technical_architecture.tool_integration: GUI-based (screenshot + mouse/keyboard) rather than API-based. This is the defining characteristic: these agents interact with any web application through its visual interface without requiring custom API integrations. OpenAI CUA is available via the Responses API for developers. Anthropic Computer Use available via API with beta header. MCP support: Anthropic ecosystem fully supports MCP; Claude for Chrome connects to Claude Code via MCP. OpenAI adopted MCP in 2025. Project Mariner integrates with Google ecosystem (Chrome, Gemini app Agent Mode).
technical_architecture.planning_approach: ReAct-style with visual grounding. The agent reasons about what it sees on screen, plans next actions, executes them, and verifies results through new screenshots. CUA uses reinforcement learning for self-correction. Mariner shares a clear outline of its decision-making process with users. Common pattern: goal decomposition -> step-by-step execution -> error detection -> self-correction -> human handoff if stuck.
technical_architecture.multi_agent_support: Limited. Most products are single-agent with task-level parallelism. Comet can spawn parallel browser agents for comparison tasks. Mariner supports up to 10 concurrent tasks (cloud VMs). Atlas agent mode handles sequential multi-step tasks. Anthropic Computer Use can be composed with other tools in multi-agent frameworks via the API but is itself a single-agent capability.

memory_and_context.memory_types_supported: short_term (conversation/session context), episodic (Atlas browser memories remembers past browsing), semantic (Dia Memory learns user preferences over time), procedural (Mariner Teach & Repeat learns workflows). Atlas stores browser memories for personalized suggestions. Dia's Memory feature builds understanding of user preferences. Comet maintains session context.
memory_and_context.context_window_management: Vision-based: each screenshot consumes significant context tokens. Anthropic Computer Use adds 466-499 tokens system prompt overhead per interaction. Agents manage context through: selective screenshot regions (Anthropic's zoom action), summarization of previous steps, maintaining action history rather than full screenshot history. Token-intensive: a single computer use session can consume hundreds of thousands of tokens.
memory_and_context.persistence_mechanism: cloud (server-side session state) + browser local storage. Atlas: cloud-based browser memories. Dia: local + cloud Memory system. Comet: session-based with cloud persistence for Max users. Mariner: cloud VMs maintain state. Operator: session-based (no persistent memory in initial release).
memory_and_context.context_engineering_approach: Critical concern for computer use agents due to high token cost per screenshot. Anthropic addresses this with the zoom action (inspect specific screen regions rather than full screenshots) and tool versioning (computer_20251124 vs computer_20250124). OpenAI CUA uses vision capabilities of GPT-4o to efficiently process screenshots. All products implement selective attention: focusing on relevant screen regions rather than processing entire screens at full resolution.

capabilities.core_capabilities: 1) Autonomous web browsing and task completion (shopping, booking, form filling, research). 2) Visual understanding of any GUI without API integration. 3) Self-correction when encountering errors. 4) Human handoff when stuck or for sensitive actions. 5) Multi-step workflow execution (browse, compare, fill forms, checkout). 6) Cross-site task orchestration (gathering info from multiple sites). Specific capabilities by product: OpenAI Operator/Atlas: agent mode for end-to-end task completion, browser memories, tab conversations. Anthropic Computer Use: full desktop control (not just browser), API access for developers, zoom action for detailed inspection. Google Mariner: 10-task parallelism, Teach & Repeat workflow learning, cloud VM execution (background tasks). Perplexity Comet: citation-rich research, parallel agent spawning for comparison tasks, background assistant. Dia: tab-based chat, custom Skills, Memory personalization, writing assistance. Benchmarks: CUA 87% WebVoyager / 58.1% WebArena / 38.1% OSWorld. Mariner 83.5% WebVoyager. Anthropic Computer Use 56% WebVoyager / 22% OSWorld.
capabilities.supported_modalities: Vision (screenshots), text, browser interaction (mouse, keyboard, scrolling, clicking). Anthropic Computer Use extends to full desktop (not browser-only). Some products support voice input (Comet, Atlas). All products are fundamentally vision + action modality.
capabilities.autonomy_level: human_in_loop to supervised. All products implement ask-before-acting for sensitive operations (purchases, form submissions, account access). Atlas: 'ChatGPT is trained to ask before taking many important actions.' Operator: hands control back to user when stuck. Mariner: keeps user informed of decision process. Full autonomy available for low-risk browsing/research tasks; approval required for transactions and account modifications.
capabilities.tool_ecosystem: Browser-native: works with any website/web application without integration. This is the key value proposition -- no API needed. OpenAI CUA available in Responses API for developer integration. Anthropic Computer Use API supports tool composition with other Claude tools. Comet built on Chromium (full extension compatibility). Atlas built on Chromium. Dia supports Chrome extensions. Mariner integrates with Google ecosystem (Search, Workspace).

agent_interoperability.mcp_support: Anthropic: Full MCP support. Claude for Chrome connects to Claude Code via MCP. Computer Use can be combined with MCP tools. OpenAI: Adopted MCP in 2025, Atlas supports MCP-connected tools. Both donated MCP to AAIF/Linux Foundation in December 2025. Google/Perplexity/Dia: No public MCP support announced, though the protocol is becoming industry standard.
agent_interoperability.a2a_support: Limited. These are primarily consumer-facing products, not agent framework components. OpenAI and Anthropic participate in the AAIF which governs both MCP and emerging agent-to-agent standards. No direct A2A protocol implementation in any agentic browser product as of February 2026.
agent_interoperability.agents_md_support: Not applicable. Agentic browsers are consumer products that interact with websites, not developer tools that read project configuration files. AGENTS.md is relevant for coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.), not browser agents.
agent_interoperability.cross_framework_compatibility: OpenAI CUA API: Can be integrated into custom agent frameworks via the Responses API (Tiers 3-5 developers). Anthropic Computer Use API: Composable with any framework that supports Claude API (LangChain, CrewAI, etc.). Both are building blocks that developers can use in larger agent systems. Consumer browser products (Atlas, Comet, Dia, Mariner) are closed ecosystems with limited cross-framework compatibility.

safety_and_guardrails.permission_model: Human-in-the-loop for sensitive actions. All products converge on a similar pattern: autonomous browsing for low-risk tasks, explicit user approval for purchases/payments/account changes/personal data entry. Atlas: trained to ask before important actions. Operator: sandbox browser environment, hands back control when stuck. Mariner: transparent decision process, user can intervene. Comet: approval prompts for transactions. Anthropic Computer Use: developer-configurable permissions via API.
safety_and_guardrails.escalation_policy: Automatic escalation to human when: 1) Agent encounters CAPTCHA or authentication challenges. 2) Financial transactions require confirmation. 3) Agent is stuck or uncertain about next steps. 4) Sensitive personal data needs to be entered. 5) Multiple possible interpretations of user intent. OpenAI Operator literally hands the browser back to the user. Atlas pauses and asks for direction.
safety_and_guardrails.hallucination_mitigation: Visual grounding reduces traditional text hallucination but introduces new failure modes. Comet occasionally 'hallucinates' data in research tasks. Common mitigations: 1) Verification loops (take action, screenshot, verify result). 2) Citation-based responses (Comet includes source links). 3) Reinforcement learning training against incorrect actions (CUA). 4) Confidence thresholds triggering human handoff. Key limitation: agents can be fooled by deceptive website content.
safety_and_guardrails.audit_trail: Session-based action logging in all products. Atlas maintains browsing history and memory. Operator provides task execution history. Anthropic Computer Use API returns structured action logs. Mariner shares step-by-step decision process with users. Developer APIs (CUA, Computer Use) return full action traces for debugging.
safety_and_guardrails.human_oversight_pattern: pre-approval for sensitive actions + always_on for monitoring. The industry has converged on Human-in-the-Loop as the primary guardrail. OpenAI acknowledges prompt injection 'may never be fully solved' for browser agents. Multi-layered approach: 1) Pre-approval for high-risk actions. 2) Continuous monitoring with intervention capability. 3) Reinforcement learning adversarial training (OpenAI uses RL-trained attacker bots). 4) Architectural isolation (sandboxed browser environments). 5) Secondary LLM critics reviewing agent actions.

governance_and_standards.governance_body: AAIF (Agentic AI Foundation) under the Linux Foundation, co-founded by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Block in December 2025. Governs MCP and related agent standards. Individual products are governed by their respective companies.
governance_and_standards.contributing_protocols: MCP (Model Context Protocol) — the dominant interoperability standard, donated to AAIF. MCP Apps Extension (joint Anthropic/OpenAI work for interactive UI capabilities). Agent Skills standard (Anthropic, December 2025). WebVoyager, WebArena, and OSWorld benchmarks serve as de facto evaluation standards for computer use agents.
governance_and_standards.regulatory_compliance: EU_AI_Act considerations: agentic browsers that make autonomous decisions on behalf of users may fall under high-risk AI system requirements depending on use case. No specific certifications announced for any product. OpenAI published research on hardening Atlas against prompt injection (December 2025). All products include privacy controls and data handling policies. Enterprise deployments (Mariner Enterprise API planned Q1 2026) will likely require SOC2 compliance.

deployment_and_operations.deployment_modes: managed_service (primary for all consumer products). Atlas: desktop app (macOS, Windows coming). Comet: desktop app (macOS, Windows) + Android. Dia: desktop app (macOS, mobile coming 2026). Mariner: cloud VMs (tasks run in background). Operator: web-based (operator.chatgpt.com). Anthropic Computer Use: cloud API (developer-managed). CUA: cloud API via Responses API.
deployment_and_operations.scalability_model: Cloud-based with per-user scaling. Mariner uses cloud VMs enabling background execution and 10-task parallelism. CUA and Computer Use APIs scale via standard API infrastructure. Consumer products scale per-user concurrency. Enterprise scalability details limited except Mariner Enterprise API (planned Q1 2026).
deployment_and_operations.cost_per_task: Varies significantly by task complexity and product. Consumer pricing: Atlas free tier (basic) to $200/month Pro (full agent mode). Comet free (core) to $200/month Max (background assistant). Dia free to $20/month Pro. Mariner: $249/month (AI Ultra subscribers). Developer API pricing: OpenAI CUA $3/1M input tokens, $12/1M output tokens. Anthropic Computer Use: standard Claude API pricing ($3/$15 per 1M tokens for Sonnet 4.5, $5/$25 for Opus 4.5) with 466-499 token overhead per interaction. A complex multi-step browsing task can consume tens of thousands of tokens, costing roughly $0.10-$1.00+ per task depending on complexity.
deployment_and_operations.resource_requirements: Consumer products: modern desktop/laptop with internet connection. Atlas/Comet/Dia require Chromium-compatible OS (macOS primary, Windows expanding). Developer APIs: standard API access, no special hardware. Mariner cloud VMs: managed by Google (no user infrastructure). Anthropic Computer Use for self-hosted: requires a computing environment with display (Docker containers with virtual displays commonly used).

observability_and_ops.monitoring_integration: Developer APIs: OpenAI CUA integrates with standard API monitoring. Anthropic Computer Use compatible with LangSmith, Langfuse, Helicone, and other LLM observability tools via API response metadata. Consumer products: built-in session history and action logs. No standardized cross-product monitoring framework exists yet.
observability_and_ops.tracing_support: Yes for developer APIs. CUA Responses API returns structured action traces. Anthropic Computer Use API provides step-by-step action logs with screenshots. Consumer products show execution history but with varying levels of detail. Mariner provides transparent step-by-step reasoning visible to users.
observability_and_ops.production_readiness_level: beta to production_ready depending on product. Atlas: production (launched Oct 2025, actively updated). Comet: production (free worldwide, active user base). Dia: beta (acquired by Atlassian, transitioning). Mariner: experimental (limited access, research prototype). Operator: deprecated/merged (integrated into ChatGPT agent mode July 2025). CUA API: beta (research preview, Tiers 3-5). Anthropic Computer Use API: beta (requires beta header). Overall category maturity: early production — functional but with known reliability and security limitations.

adoption_and_market.github_stars: Not directly applicable (proprietary products). Related open-source alternatives: Open Operator (Browserbase) ~1,700+ stars. browser-use (open-source browser agent) ~60,000+ stars. Agent S (Simular AI) growing. OpenAI Agents SDK ~18,000+ stars.
adoption_and_market.adoption_scale: Comet: 10 million monthly active users (Q3 2025), enterprise deployments grew 200% in H1 2025. Atlas: launched to all ChatGPT tiers (Free, Plus, Pro, Go, Business, Enterprise) worldwide on macOS. ChatGPT has 400M+ weekly active users (as of early 2026), with Atlas as its default browser. Mariner: limited access (AI Ultra subscribers, US only). Dia: early adoption, exact numbers not disclosed. Agentic browser market: $4.5B (2024) growing at 32.8% CAGR to projected $76.8B by 2034.
adoption_and_market.pricing_model: Freemium (dominant model). Atlas: free basic, $20/month Plus for agent mode, $200/month Pro. Comet: free core, $5/month Plus, $200/month Max. Dia: free core, $20/month Pro. Mariner: $249/month (AI Ultra). Developer APIs: per-token pricing (CUA: $3/$12 per 1M tokens; Computer Use: standard Claude pricing). Operator: was $200/month Pro-only, now merged into ChatGPT agent mode.
adoption_and_market.key_use_cases: 1) Online shopping and price comparison (browse multiple sites, compare products, add to cart). 2) Travel booking (search flights, hotels, compare options). 3) Research and information gathering (multi-source synthesis with citations). 4) Form filling and data entry (automate repetitive web forms). 5) Email and calendar management (triage, draft responses, schedule). 6) Job searching and application (find listings, fill applications). 7) Enterprise workflow automation (navigate internal SaaS tools). 8) Content creation and publishing (draft, edit, post across platforms). Industries: e-commerce, travel, enterprise productivity, customer service, market research.
adoption_and_market.competitive_position: Three-tier market structure: 1) AI-native browsers (Atlas, Comet, Dia) — standalone browsers with AI deeply integrated, competing for default browser position. 2) Agent overlays (Operator/ChatGPT agent mode, Mariner) — AI agents that control existing browsers or run in cloud VMs. 3) Developer APIs (CUA, Computer Use) — building blocks for custom computer use agents. OpenAI leads with dual strategy (Atlas browser + CUA API + ChatGPT agent mode). Google defends Chrome dominance with Mariner + Chrome Auto Browse. Anthropic focuses on developer API rather than consumer browser. Perplexity differentiates on research/citation quality. Dia/Atlassian pivoting to enterprise collaboration browser.

ecosystem_maturity.community_size: Massive backing from major AI companies. OpenAI community (millions of developers). Anthropic developer ecosystem (growing rapidly with MCP adoption: 3,000+ MCP servers). Google AI developer community. Dedicated agentic browser communities are still nascent. Security research community actively probing these products (Brave, Wiz, LayerX, Guardio Labs publishing vulnerability research).
ecosystem_maturity.documentation_quality: good to excellent for developer APIs. OpenAI CUA: documented in Responses API docs. Anthropic Computer Use: comprehensive API documentation with tool specifications. Consumer products: adequate user documentation. Security best practices documentation growing (OpenAI published hardening guide for Atlas). Overall: documentation is strong for APIs, less detailed for consumer product internals.
ecosystem_maturity.third_party_integrations_count: Browser-based products inherit the entire web as their integration surface — they work with any website. Chromium-based browsers (Atlas, Comet, Dia) support Chrome extensions. Developer APIs support composition with other tools. MCP ecosystem provides 3,000+ server integrations for Anthropic stack. Specific integration counts not published for most products.
ecosystem_maturity.tutorial_availability: good. Multiple comparison guides and tutorials published by tech media (TechCrunch, MarkTechPost, AIMultiple). Anthropic provides computer use quickstart guides and reference implementations on GitHub. OpenAI provides CUA starter kit. Third-party tutorials widely available. DataCamp, Skywork, and others publish step-by-step guides. Still early for advanced/enterprise tutorials.

human_agent_interaction.autonomy_spectrum: assistant (executes with approval) for most products. Atlas and Comet approach autonomous for low-risk research tasks but revert to assistant for transactions. Mariner and Operator are supervised (transparent step display). Dia is copilot (suggestions and chat, limited autonomous action). Anthropic Computer Use is developer-configurable from copilot to autonomous depending on implementation.
human_agent_interaction.handoff_mechanism: Seamless browser control transfer. Operator literally returns browser control to the user when stuck. Atlas pauses agent mode and prompts user for guidance. Mariner shows reasoning and asks for input at decision points. Comet prompts for confirmation on sensitive actions. Anthropic Computer Use: developer-configurable handoff via API (can implement custom escalation logic). All products maintain the principle that users can interrupt, pause, or take over at any time.
human_agent_interaction.feedback_loop: Atlas: browser memories learn from past interactions and suggest relevant content. Dia: Memory feature builds understanding of user preferences over time. Mariner: Teach & Repeat learns user workflows. Comet: session-based learning within interactions. Anthropic Computer Use: no built-in feedback loop (developer responsibility). CUA trained via reinforcement learning from human feedback during development. User feedback mechanisms vary: Atlas and Dia have persistent memory, others are more session-scoped.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: High relevance for entrepreneurs in 2026. Key considerations: 1) IMMEDIATE USE: Entrepreneurs can use agentic browsers today for market research (Comet excels at multi-source research with citations), competitive analysis, lead generation, and automating repetitive web tasks (form filling, data extraction, booking). 2) BUILD OPPORTUNITIES: The CUA and Computer Use APIs enable startups to build specialized computer use agents for vertical markets (real estate, recruiting, e-commerce, compliance). Developer API pricing ($3-12/1M tokens) makes prototyping affordable. 3) INTEGRATION PLAY: Build on top of agentic browsers rather than competing — create Skills for Dia, extensions for Atlas/Comet, or MCP servers that enhance computer use agents. 4) SECURITY OPPORTUNITY: The acknowledged prompt injection vulnerability creates opportunity for security startups (Seraphic Security, LayerX already in this space). 5) WHEN TO AVOID: Don't build a general-purpose agentic browser — the market is dominated by OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, and Perplexity. Don't rely on agentic browsers for mission-critical financial transactions yet (reliability 38-87% depending on task complexity). 6) ENTERPRISE ANGLE: 76.8% of the AI browser market is enterprise-focused. Building enterprise-specific computer use agents (navigating internal tools, automating compliance workflows) is a defensible niche. The Atlassian acquisition of Dia ($610M) validates the enterprise browser agent thesis.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy: BUY for most startups. Use existing agentic browsers (Atlas, Comet free tier) for internal productivity. BUILD custom agents only if: 1) You need specialized domain expertise (e.g., healthcare workflow automation). 2) You need reliable, repeatable automation for a specific workflow. 3) You can tolerate current reliability limitations (38-87% success rates). 4) You have API access (CUA Tiers 3-5, Computer Use API). Cost comparison: Consumer browser ($0-200/month) vs. API-based custom agent ($0.10-1.00/task at scale) vs. building from scratch (significant engineering investment). The open-source alternatives (browser-use with 60K+ GitHub stars) provide a middle ground for technical teams.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & No-Code Tools): agentic browsers as advanced prompting interfaces, hands-on with Comet/Atlas for research tasks. Session 3 (AI Project Framing): computer use APIs as build-vs-buy case study, cost analysis of API pricing. Session 4 (Business Models): freemium model analysis (Atlas/Comet pricing tiers), enterprise market opportunity ($76.8B by 2034), Atlassian-Dia acquisition as M&A case study. Session 5 (Ethics & Governance): prompt injection security risks, human oversight patterns, EU AI Act implications for autonomous web agents.

confidence.data_quality: High for product features and pricing (sourced from official announcements and reputable tech media). Medium for market size projections (varies by source). Medium for benchmark scores (may be updated as models improve).
confidence.cross_reference: OpenAI official blog + TechCrunch + MIT Technology Review confirm Operator/CUA/Atlas details. Anthropic official docs + API documentation confirm Computer Use specifications. Google DeepMind + TechCrunch + Google I/O announcements confirm Mariner details. Multiple TechCrunch articles + BusinessWire confirm Dia/Atlassian acquisition ($610M). Wiz, Brave, OpenAI security research confirm prompt injection concerns. AIMultiple, BrightData, MarkTechPost comparison guides cross-validate feature comparisons.
confidence.caveats: 1) RAPIDLY EVOLVING: This market is moving extremely fast. Operator was merged into ChatGPT agent mode within 6 months of launch. Products may be renamed, merged, or discontinued. 2) BENCHMARK LIMITATIONS: WebVoyager/OSWorld scores vary by model version and may not reflect real-world reliability. Human success rate on OSWorld is 72.4% vs. best AI at 38.1%. 3) SECURITY UNRESOLVED: OpenAI publicly acknowledged prompt injection may never be fully solved for browser agents. This is a fundamental architectural limitation. 4) PRICING FLUX: Comet went from $200/month to free in 3 months. Pricing strategies are still being established. 5) ENTERPRISE MATURITY: Despite strong adoption numbers, enterprise-grade features (SSO, audit logs, compliance certifications) are still being developed. 6) GEOGRAPHIC LIMITS: Many products US-only or macOS-first initially. 7) The Dia acquisition by Atlassian ($610M) may significantly change its product direction toward enterprise collaboration.
